chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from Al-Washa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Arta'ah ibn Habib Al-Asadi, from a man, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who is exceeded against with regards to a charity of his wealth, so he fights and is killed, so he is a martyr.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone killed while defending their charity from oppression?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies that defending one's wealth (*mal*) from unjust seizure (*i'tiday*) is a legitimate act of self-defense, granting the defender the high spiritual status of a martyr (*shahid*) upon death. This ruling underscores the sanctity of property rights in Islam and distinguishes this specific defense from general jihad, emphasizing that the intent to preserve one's lawful estate validates the martyrdom reward.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad, from Al Washa, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Artaat Bin Habeeb Al Asady, from a man,

(It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who is exceeded against with regards to a charity of his wealth, so he fights and is killed, so he is a martyr’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Ahmad from al-Washsha’ from Safwan ibn Yahya from Artat ibn Habib al-Asadiy from a man from Ali ibn Al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, , who has said the following: “
If one is subjected to transgression over the charity of his property and he fights back and is murdered he is a martyr.”
